briefing.text: In endometrial cancer, race is strongly confounded with histology and molecular subtype: published ancestry analyses (e.g. TCGA UCEC) report more serous/clear-cell and CN-high/TP53-abnormal tumours in Black patients and more endometrioid MMRd/MSI-H and POLE tumours in White patients. Cross-tabulate RACE (patient file) against MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE and histology (sample file) for Black vs White, report crude rates and rates stratified by histology, and state whether the observed direction agrees with this background.
briefing.reason: Subtype mix differs sharply by race, so crude comparisons of MSI-H/TMB-H or actionability can reflect histology; teams need to check and report direction against established biology.

briefing.text: There may be no separate MSI column. Print the unique MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE values; if it holds TCGA/ProMisE-style classes (POLE, MMRd/MSI-H, CN-low/NSMP, CN-high/TP53abn), use the MMRd/MSI-H class as MSI-H and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS >= 10 mut/Mb as TMB-high (FDA tumour-agnostic pembrolizumab cutoff). Define combined TMB-H/MSI-H as MSI-H OR POLE OR TMB>=10, and also report each component separately, because POLE tumours are TMB-high but not MSI-H.
briefing.reason: Determines how the hypothesis's key endpoint is operationalised from the available columns.

briefing.text: Samples were sequenced on different MSK-IMPACT panel versions (IMPACT341/410/468/505) covering different megabases, so raw mutation counts from data_mutations.txt are not comparable. Use the per-Mb TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS column, confirm its values look per-Mb (low single digits for serous, >10 for MSI-H), cross-tabulate GENE_PANEL by race, and if the panel mix differs by race check that the result holds within panel. (Normalisation details are from domain knowledge, not verified.)
briefing.reason: Panel mix can differ by race and bias TMB comparisons if counts are used.

briefing.text: Some patients have multiple samples and RACE includes Asian/Other/Unknown values. Keep one sample per patient (prefer primary; join sample file to patient file on PATIENT_ID), compare Black vs White only, and test pre-specified binary endpoints (MSI-H/MMRd, TMB>=10, combined TMB-H/MSI-H, any actionable alteration) with Fisher exact/chi-square plus logistic regression adjusted for histology. If you scan many genes, apply BH correction and do not base the conclusion on gene-level hits. Report direction and p-value.
briefing.reason: Unit of analysis, group definition and multiple testing directly affect the rates compared.

briefing.text: 'Clinically actionable' needs a defined knowledge base: MSK cohort studies usually call a tumour actionable if it has at least one OncoKB Level 1-3 (sometimes 1-3B) alteration. Relevant calls include tumour-agnostic MSI-H, TMB-H (>=10 mut/Mb) and NTRK1/2/3 fusions, plus ERBB2 amplification (CNA=2; trastuzumab in serous EC), PIK3CA oncogenic/hotspot mutations, BRCA1/2 oncogenic/truncating mutations and KRAS G12C. Counting any mutation inflates actionability, especially in hypermutated tumours. Build a per-patient flag from this short list and report actionability both with and without MSI-H/TMB-H. ERBB2 amplification, which is more common in serous tumours, can move composite actionability in a different direction from MSI-H/TMB-H, so report the components separately as well as together. (Not web-verified.)
briefing.reason: The hypothesis bundles composite actionability with TMB-H/MSI-H; how actionability is defined and decomposed can change the comparison.

shared_assumptions: Self-reported RACE (Black vs White) is the grouping the hypothesis means; the cohort is an 'ancestry' cohort and neither team asked whether genetic ancestry vs self-report could reclassify patients, nor how Hispanic Black/White patients (13 and 92) and 'Unknown' ethnicity should be handled.

TMB-H is TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS >= 10 per Mb across all panels (IMPACT341/410/468/505) and MSI-H is taken from MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE; neither tested whether POLE-subtype tumours (also TMB-high) were counted consistently in the TMB-H/MSI-H endpoint.
Both treat one sample per patient as independent and pool Primary and Recurrence samples (team B only ran a primary-only check, team A did not).
unused_evidence: data_mutations.txt carries OncoKB annotation columns (HIGHEST_LEVEL, LEVEL_1..LEVEL_4, LEVEL_R*, ONCOGENIC, VARIANT_IN_ONCOKB, Annotation_Status=SUCCESS for all rows). Team B states there is no OncoKB annotation and team A built an 'OncoKB-like' flag; the deposited levels were not used to define 'clinically actionable'.
data_gene_panel_matrix.txt distinguishes mutation vs CNA panels per sample; neither team says it used it to restrict actionable-gene calls to genes actually covered by each sample's panel.
ETHNICITY column was not used in any sensitivity check.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named the actionability definition as their weakest point and only reported it; neither rebuilt it from the deposited OncoKB level columns.
Team A: after histology adjustment the TMB-H/MSI-H difference is borderline (OR 0.69, p~0.06); reported, not resolved as to which quantity the hypothesis concerns.
ERBB2 amplification runs opposite (higher in Black patients); both reported it but the composite's direction may depend on how ERBB2 amp and levels 3/4 alterations are weighted.
second_readings: 'Clinically actionable alterations' may mean OncoKB level 1-3 alterations (therapeutic levels) rather than any alteration in a druggable gene; under a strict level definition the composite could be dominated by ERBB2 amplification in serous tumours, which is enriched in Black patients.
'More frequent' could be read as crude frequency (what both teams used) or as frequency within histology/molecular subtype; the direction is the same in both teams' reports, but magnitude differs.
The grouping could be genetic ancestry (African vs European) rather than self-reported race; only self-reported race is in the tables.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed answer fairly well: the TMB-H/MSI-H component is large, consistent across panels and both teams, and runs opposite to the claim; the main open risk is the actionability composite, which both built without the deposited OncoKB levels and which has an opposing ERBB2 signal.

If you redefine 'any actionable alteration' from these deposited levels (e.g., levels 1-3A only vs including 3B/4), plus ERBB2 amplification from data_cna.txt and TMB-H/MSI-H, does the Black-vs-White direction of the composite change?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: How did you treat POLE-subtype tumours in the TMB-H/MSI-H endpoint, and does counting them in or out of 'TMB-H' change the Black-vs-White comparison?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your weakest point says there is no OncoKB annotation, but data_mutations.txt has HIGHEST_LEVEL and LEVEL_* columns with Annotation_Status SUCCESS. If you rebuild the actionable flag from those levels (with ERBB2 amplification from CNA), does the composite still run lower in Black patients?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Does excluding Hispanic and Unknown-ethnicity patients, or excluding POLE-subtype tumours from TMB-H, change the direction of the TMB-H/MSI-H difference between Black and White patients?

questions.why: Both teams approximated actionability; the deposited level columns could define it directly, and the cutoff choice may move the composite.

questions.question: In cBioPortal-style MAF files annotated by the OncoKB annotator, does HIGHEST_LEVEL include tumour-agnostic biomarkers such as TMB-H or MSI-H, or only variant-level levels, and are copy-number amplifications annotated separately?
questions.why: Determines whether TMB-H/MSI-H and ERBB2 amplification must be added to the mutation-level actionable flag or would be double-counted.

findings.question: How are OncoKB therapeutic levels of evidence (1, 2, 3A, 3B, 4, R1, R2) defined, and which levels do clinical-genomics papers usually count as 'clinically actionable'?
findings.answer: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the research gateway returned HTTP 403 on every call, so this is domain knowledge. Level 1 = FDA-recognised biomarker predicting response to an FDA-approved drug in this indication; Level 2 = standard-care (NCCN or other guideline) biomarker predicting response to an FDA-approved drug in this indication; Level 3A = compelling clinical evidence of response in this indication; Level 3B = standard-care or investigational biomarker predicting response in another indication; Level 4 = compelling biological evidence only; R1 = standard-care resistance biomarker in this indication; R2 = compelling clinical evidence of resistance. Most clinical-genomics (MSK) papers count Level 1-3B as 'clinically actionable'. Some report Level 1-2 as standard-care actionable. Level 4 is reported separately and R levels are excluded.

findings.question: In cBioPortal-style MAF files annotated by the OncoKB annotator, does HIGHEST_LEVEL include tumour-agnostic biomarkers such as TMB-H or MSI-H, or only variant-level levels, and are copy-number amplifications annotated separately?
findings.answer: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the research gateway returned HTTP 403, so this is domain knowledge. MafAnnotator's HIGHEST_LEVEL is per mutation row and covers only that variant. It does not include TMB-H or MSI-H, which OncoKB queries as separate 'Other Biomarkers'. CNAs such as ERBB2 amplification are annotated separately by CnaAnnotator, and fusions by FusionAnnotator. ClinicalDataAnnotator combines these into a per-sample level. So ERBB2 amplification (data_cna.txt, value 2) and TMB-H/MSI-H (clinical columns) must be added to the mutation-level flag, and adding them will not double-count.
